pages.text: The molecular assembler takes items input into it and carries out the operation defined by an adjacent $(l:items_blocks_machines/pattern_provider)ME Pattern Provider$(/l), or the inserted $(l:items_blocks_machines/patterns)Crafting Pattern$(/l), $(l:items_blocks_machines/patterns)Smithing Table Pattern$(/l), or $(l:items_blocks_machines/patterns)Stonecutting Pattern$(/l), then pushes the result to adjacent inventories.$(br2)This assembler has a crafting pattern that specifies the 1
oak log = 4 oak planks recipe. When oak logs are fed into the upper hopper, the assembler crafts and spits oak planks into the lower hopper.
$(bold)The Main Use Of The Molecular Assembler$()

However, their main use is next to a $(l:items_blocks_machines/pattern_provider)ME Pattern Provider$(/l). Pattern providers have special behavior in this case, and will send information about the relevant pattern along with the ingredients to adjacent assemblers. Since assemblers auto-eject the results of crafts to adjacent inventories (and thus into the return slots of the pattern provider), an assembler on a pattern provider is all that is needed to automate crafting patterns.

pages.title: Upgrades
pages.text: The Molecular Assembler supports the following $(l:items_blocks_machines/upgrade_cards)upgrades$(/l):$(li)$(l:items_blocks_machines/upgrade_cards)Acceleration Card$(/l)

pages.title: Note
pages.text: Optifine breaks the "push to adjacent inventories" function so most crafting setups with assemblers won't work.
